title: Research opportunities to avoid texture copies
description:
GTK uses wl_shm, which means that phoc ends up uploading every damaged part of the frame to GL domain with `glTex(Sub)Image2D`. Just keeping up with fullscreen updates of wl_shm surfaces makes phoc take more than 30% of devkit's CPU core time.

Given that we don't have dedicated VRAM, theoretically it might be possible to avoid copies and just share the shared memory buffer with the GL driver. Whether it's actually possible in practice remains to be seen.

More or less related reading:
- https://software.intel.com/en-us/articles/zero-copy-texture-uploads-in-chrome-os
- https://01.org/chromium/2016/native-one-copy-texture-uploads-for-chrome-OS
- https://arrayfire.com/zero-copy-on-integrated-gpus/
- https://events17.linuxfoundation.org/sites/events/files/slides/ELC17-virtmem-exp_0.pdf (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LFU39w7lY08) - code: https://github.com/jaychiang001/tda2_kernel/commit/c940bbbdfa32d492eddbc255459bc505dff7bef5

title: XWayland touch events are somehow broken with SDL2, its touch mouse emulation doesn't work
description:
Ok, so since there seems to be so far no progress on the keyboard input being broken with SDL2 with Wayland ( https://source.puri.sm/Librem5/squeekboard/-/issues/218 ) I am sadly finding myself unable to use a quite complex SDL2 app since the XWayland mode with SDL2 also has a quite notable input breakage: in XWayland touch events are somehow broken with SDL2, it's mouse emulation (SDL_TOUCH_MOUSEID) just plain doesn't seem to work. This makes applications relying on this unusable.

However, SDL2's mouse emulation *does* work under Phosh+Wayland, so this seems to be some XWayland+Phosh+Phoc interaction issue, or a bug in SDL2's XWayland code. In any case, it would be great if *either* the XWayland input handling, *or* the Wayland input handling worked properly with Phosh, which sadly is not the case. I never had any issues on my x64 desktop with GNOME 3 or on Android, so this is sadly limited to PinePhone+Phosh (and likely Librem 5 I would assume) same as the broken Wayland input. I'm not sure what mode the desktop used (Wayland/XWayland), but it works.

To reproduce, set the hints:

SDL_ANDROID_SEPARATE_MOUSE_AND_TOUCH=1

SDL_MOUSE_TOUCH_EVENTS=0

SDL_TOUCH_MOUSE_EVENTS=1

SDL_VIDEODRIVER=x11

Then, run a minimal SDL2 app that just prints out the event queue. Correct behavior is:

1. Any hardware mouse input generates events SDL_MOUSEMOTION/SDL_MOUSEBUTTONDOWN/SDL_MOUSEBUTTONUP with which != SDL_TOUCH_MOUSEID on all of these. No touch events are generated for these.
2. Any touch event generates SDL_FINGERDOWN/SDL_FINGERUP/SDL_FINGERMOTION **and** the above of SDL_MOUSEMOTION/SDL_MOUSEBUTTONDOWN/SDL_MOUSEBUTTONUP with which == SDL_TOUCH_MOUSEID (emulating a single finger with SDL2's emulation, with multi touch gestures this usually follows the first finger that touched the screen).

The second point is broken under Phosh+Xwayland, the single finger emulation is from what I can tell simply missing **except for the first finger tap**. (So it breaks e.g. if you tap twice, and then is just broken with all which == SDL_TOUCH_MOUSEID events missing until you restart the app). If you modify the above example to use SDL_VIDEODRIVER=wayland you'll see it suddenly works, but now all SDL_KEYDOWN/SDL_KEYUP events are completely garbled. Sadly, this leaves both modes without event handling working as it should.

Device info/tested on: PinePhone Manjaro Ed., running Mobian/Debian & Phosh

title: Traditional Alt-Tab behavior
description:
Currently window cycling in phosh / phoc works like a normal shortcut: (I'll assume that the key combination is Alt-Tab here) Windows are cycled in order through the focus queue and it does not matter if Alt is raised between presses or not.

The [Alt-Tab article in wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alt-Tab#Behavior) explains the traditional behaviour well, but the main gist is that holding down Alt and pressing Tab (repeatedly) raises and selects the next window in focus queue and only when Alt is raised, is the selected window brought to the front of the queue and focused.

Also, since the overview in phosh presents windows linearly, the order of the windows there could match the focus queue.

title: input-method-v2 not setting cursor correctly
description: I noticed that when using the virtual-keyboard protocol with the input-method protocol the cursor is not moved as expected. This works as expected but if you also use virtual-keyboard to send a keycode to the compositor the offset is no longer correct. Each time a keycode is sent the compositor also replies with a surrounding_text event but does not update the cursor offset. If afterwards a response from the input-method protocol is sent, the cursor offset gets updated and is correct.

title: Better support xwaylandvideobridge
description:
The above program show a bunch of shortcomings in our X11 handling

- [x] It uses `setOpacity(0)` but the surface isn't made transparent (the relevant ATOM seems to be `_NET_WM_WINDOW_OPACITY`) (See [this wlroots MR](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/wlroots/wlroots/-/merge_requests/4995) and !660)
- [ ] It uses `_GTK_FRAME_EXTENTS` to move itself "almost" off screen which wlroots / phoc doesn't handle (see also !659) but not at all standerized so unlikely to get supported.
- [ ] It uses `KX11Extras::setState(winId(), NET::SkipSwitcher)` so we should switch it on `AltTab` (uses `_KDE_NET_WM_STATE_SKIP_SWITCHER` so not standarized)
- [ ] It uses  `KX11Extras::setState(winId(), NET::SkipTaskbar);` so it shouldn't show up in phosh's overview (uses `_NET_WM_STATE_SKIP_TASKBAR` which is part of the [wm-spec](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/wm-spec/latest-single/) but no Wayland protocol supports forwarding that information to clients yet (https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/wayland/wayland-protocols/-/merge_requests/196#note_2812516)

Filing this here as everything fixed would improve X11 / XWayland in case someone is interested in that.

title: Activation tokens may get lost before mapping
description:
Looking at why GNOME Calendar's splash sometimes times out, I noticed that sometimes after redeeming the token it receives from platform data it immediately generates a new one.

```
[2943843.122]  -> xdg_activation_v1@14.activate("f0341f6ecdae8adebeeee5cd184e5b13", wl_surface@28)
[2943848.173]  -> xdg_activation_v1@14.get_activation_token(new id xdg_activation_token_v1@42)
[2943848.228]  -> xdg_activation_token_v1@42.set_serial(2399, wl_seat@22)
[2943848.246]  -> xdg_activation_token_v1@42.commit()
[2943849.112] xdg_activation_token_v1@42.done("918ae83de62131a14886a32ce6c0dc0f")
[2943849.139]  -> xdg_activation_token_v1@42.destroy()
[2943849.157]  -> xdg_activation_v1@14.activate("918ae83de62131a14886a32ce6c0dc0f", wl_surface@28)
```

As both of these activations get sent before mapping, the second call to `phoc_view_set_activation_token` overwrites the first one, which then never reaches Phosh, so the splash doesn't get hidden until it times out.

title: Improve scale-to-fit logic
description:
Currently scale-to-fit scales down the view when it doesn't fit, but it doesn't make any attempt to scale it out back once it becomes possible again. This can lead to unnecessarily scaled windows when interacting with things like screen rotation, keyboard's exclusive zone, multiple screens or even just changing window's content; and the only way to reset back to normal scale is to close and open the window again.

It would be good to make sure the application is always given a chance to reset its scale to 1 whenever possible (a set of unit tests may be a great addition to that too).

title: Bottom bar gesture to bring the whole screen down, accommodating single hand use
description:
I am using Phosh on OnePlus 6, which has a very elongated screen. This means that it's impossible for me to reach upper 1/3 of the screen with my right thumb. Could we add a gesture or a double tap on the bottom bar that would simply offset the root window vertically by some amount and move it down within thumb reach? iOS has this feature and it works wonders for single handed use, see https://support.apple.com/en-au/guide/iphone/iph77bcdd132/13.0/ios/13.0#iph145eba8e9

Ideally, if we know the physical display dimensions of the device, we could use some math to move the top of the screen to some fixed distance (average thumb size?) in actual centimeters from the bottom edge.

Some more thoughts: Even though iOS has this bound to a home button double tap, on my iPhone SE which has a slightly recessed home button, I've discovered that a quick "smear" gesture (swipe right, back to left then right again) over home button gets recognized as double tap instead. This gesture is bit more ergonomic than double tap as it's smother to execute and doesn't resulting a rocking motion of the phone which can be fatiguing, esp. if the unit in use is very top-heavy.

title: Take window decorations into account when maximizing
description:
Currently we don't show server side window decorations when maximizing windows. This is fine for auto-maximize but we should draw them (and thus make the window a bit smaller) in non auto-maximize mode.

Related: https://gitlab.gnome.org/World/Phosh/phoc/-/merge_requests/570

title: Odd seat <-> cursor split
description:
The seat has a cursor however the cursor's listeners aren't connected in it's module but rather in the seat module but some of them are then proxied over to the cursor while others (e.g. handle_tablet_tool_position) are handled in seat.c directly.

Looks as if the whole `handle_cursor_` handling for `wlr_cursor` events could be moved over into `cursor.c` and then just have the cursor emit a "activity" signal so the seat can emit `wlr_idle_notify_activity()`.

title: phoc computes a scale factor that is too large for phosh on devices with 16:9 resolution and 300 DPI
description:
This is a continuation of World/Phosh/phosh#1055

My samsung-a5 computes a scale factor of 2.0:

```
G_MESSAGES_DEBUG="phoc-utils" phoc -E glxgears
Running compositor on wayland display 'wayland-0'

(phoc:1362): phoc-wlroots-CRITICAL **: 16:28:03.813: [backend/drm/util.c:66] Failed to parse EDID
phoc-output-Message: 16:28:03.815: Output 'DSI-1' added ('(null)'/'(null)'/'(null)'), 62mm x 110mm
(phoc:1362): phoc-utils-DEBUG: 16:28:03.826: Output DPI is 295.563660 for mode 720x1280, using scale 2.000000
```

According to the [specs](https://www.gsmarena.com/samsung_galaxy_a5-6761.php) for this device, the calculated ~300 dpi is correct. The problem is that a scale factor of `2.0` with a native vertical resolution of 1280 means that the effective vertical resolution is 640.

@guidog noted the following in World/Phosh/phosh#1055:

> 1280/2 = 640 which is \< 720 so this is expected and the lock screen is just the most visible place where this goes wrong.

If 720 is the magical minimum vertical resolution that phosh cares about, should we codify that somewhere?

For example, maybe we could add a `minimum_vertical_resolution` config (and default it to `720`) to `phoc.ini`, and ensure that `phoc_utils_compute_scale` never produces a scale factor that goes below that minimum amount.

title: Robustness feature request: make phoc restart when lima device driver trashes its GL context
description:
On lima GPUs like on the PinePhone, it appears like various conditions like [a currently unfixed bug](https://gitlab.com/postmarketOS/pmaports/-/issues/805) can make the GL context of phoc get marked as permanently invalid. This currently in practice makes the device appear hung to the user, requiring a hard reset. (TTY access or SSH also works, but the average user probably wouldn't know.) As I understand it, per lima GPU hw design this happening is unavoidable even if the bug making it more common is fixed because the GPU appears to be processing applications sequentially and to not have a malicious application make it get stuck for all others it has this timeout that marks apps' glcontexts as invalid. But this might mean in particular apps could try to slow down phoc's drawing intentionally to make it hit this condition, and have it get stuck in this invalid mode for a denial of service of the device.

Therefore, I think it would be a huge improvement if phoc detected this GL context trashing happening and reacted with a restart. This would avoid file system level data loss and even sd card hw damage risks caused by a full device reset initiated by a trapped user, and improve the outcome to only app level data loss by restarting the session. This would also greatly reduce the downtime and period of unreachability caused by a full device reset.

**Tested with phoc version:** 0.26.0

**Tested on device:** PinePhone Allwinner (3GB RAM model)

**Tested on linux distribution:** postmarketOS 22.12, based on Alpine Linux

title: Autoscaling results in resolution lower than that phosh requires
description:
Basically copied the following text from https://gitlab.gnome.org/World/Phosh/phoc/-/merge_requests/361#note_1546151:

Problem: On my Xiaomi Redmi 2 (`Xiaomi Redmi 2: size 59 x 104 mm / mode 720 x 1280 px`), I am [having troubles](https://gitlab.gnome.org/World/Phosh/phosh/-/issues/833) with lock screen (and actually some apps) under 200% scaling. For example the unlock button is almost out of the screen.

According to https://gitlab.gnome.org/World/Phosh/phosh/-/issues/833#note_1546078, the minimal supported resolution by phosh is 360x720. While during computing autoscaling in https://gitlab.gnome.org/World/Phosh/phoc/-/merge_requests/361/diffs#564acd062af6863aeb3ffd0ae93062d7600ce3bb_96_100, minimal height is set to 540:
```c
#define MIN_HEIGHT      540.0
```

Thus, in my case, the autoscaling will be 2. But the height 1280/2=640 will be below the minimal requirement of 720.

This won't affect recent phones with aspect ratio more than 2:1, since `#define MIN_WIDTH       360.0` will be used, thus the resulting resolution will be more than 360x720. But for small 16:9 screens, `MIN_HEIGHT` will be used to calculate the scaling and the case above might happen.

title: Not clear how to move windows
description:
It's not always clear how windows can be moved when an external display is attached.

## How to reproduce

1. Attach an external display
2. Bring up application list
3. Click Gnome Web
4. Try moving it to the external display

## What is the current behaviour?

![20211122_14h51m50s_grim](/uploads/49c251207c0c84175614e887272098e8/20211122_14h51m50s_grim.png)

(This is a screenshot from undocked mode, but it's identical in docked mode AFAICT.)

I don't know how to move this window.

## What is the expected behaviour?

I'm not sure. There should always be some cue to indicate that windows can be placed on the other screen.

## Notes

Offloading the cue for moving to applications will result in inconsistency.

Perhaps the solution is to change something about the presentation of the screen contents when in floating mode. That change will stand out, and as such become a cue.

On server-side-decorated systems, tiling managers usually skip decorations, and floating managers have them, and so the presence of decorations is a natural cue as for which mode is active.

Since the headerbar takes the role of decorations, perhaps something should change there. (That would still not solve the issue of inconsistent applications.)

Perhaps the compositor should do something, like automatically lay out windows on the external screen when enabled. That would have forced thinking about how to move them, at the cost of being unexpected.

```
  Phosh Version: 0.14.0-1pureos1
```

L5 Evergreen

title: Enable app-drawer widget at the bottom to autohide
description:
TLDR: I'd like the app-drawer to behave like the one on PlasmaMobile. Auto-hide and give full-screen to apps. If you need it, you swipe up and there it is.

**Details**

Once #82 is fixed (or before if it's already possible), it would be nice to have the option for the bottom app-drawer widget (the black rectangle with an ^) to auto-hide and be made visible again via a swipe from bottom to top (also to get the show/hide keyboard button).

Making it auto-hide would have several advantages:

1. avoid clicking by mistake on the widget while typing (Phosh [#412](https://gitlab.gnome.org/World/Phosh/phosh/-/issues/412))
2. avoid bad interaction with fullscreen apps that have buttons at the bottom (e.g. videos in web browsers)
3. issues with Waydroid as the widget hides the bottom of the android apps (keyboard or back/home buttons, though this might have been fixed by !302, I need to check in more details)

In the absence of gestures, I also wonder whether it could be possible to detect clicks at the bottom of the screen, in the middle (where there usually are no button, so we don't get point 2 all over again.
